description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. If you choose a feat, such as [Great Weapon Fighting](https://5e.tools/feats.html#great%20weapon%20fighting_xphb), that requires you to hold a Melee weapon in one or two hands, you can use that feat with Ranged weapons.
Whenever you gain a Gunslinger level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.
You're adept at drawing and firing before others have time to react, granting you the following benefits.

description.name: Initiative
description.value: You have Advantage on Initiative rolls.

description.name: Double Draw
description.value: You can draw or stow two weapons that lack Two-Handed when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Ranged weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Gunslinger levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Gunslinger Features table.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: Your attack rolls with Ranged weapons can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
At Gunslinger level 9, your attack rolls with Ranged weapons score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20. At Gunslinger level 17, they score a Critical Hit on a roll of 17-20.
You can perform incredible feats of daring fueled by special dice called Risk Dice.

description.name: Risk Dice
description.value: You have four Risk Dice, which are d8s. A Risk Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Risk Dice when you finish a Short or Long Rest. Your Risk Die changes and more Risk Dice become available as shown on the Risk Dice column of the Gunslinger Features table.

description.name: Maneuvers
description.value: You can expend Risk Dice to perform maneuvers. Your maneuver options are detailed later in the class description.

description.name: Saving Throws
description.value: If a maneuver requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus.

description.name: Maneuver Options
description.value:
• Bite the Bullet (ValdaGunslinger)
• Blindfire (ValdaGunslinger)
• Dodge Roll (ValdaGunslinger)
• Grazing Shot (ValdaGunslinger)
• Maverick Spirit (ValdaGunslinger)
• Skin of Your Teeth (ValdaGunslinger)

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain a Gunslinger subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Gunslinger levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Gunslinger level or lower.

Whenever you score a Critical Hit against a Large or smaller creature with a ranged attack using a weapon, the projectile lodges itself in the target. For 1 minute or until the target replaces one of its attacks with dislodging the projectile, its Speed is halved and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.
You don't benefit from this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: Your attack rolls with Ranged weapons can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18, 19, or 20 on the d20.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: When you deal damage with a Ranged weapon that doesn't add your ability modifier to the roll, you add your ability modifier nonetheless. If you already add your modifier to the damage roll, the target takes an extra **1d8** damage of the weapon's type.
Note that weapons that have the Firearm property don't add your ability modifier to damage rolls.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points and not killed outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead, and you regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Gunslinger level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: Whenever you roll Initiative or score a Critical Hit, you regain one expended Risk.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: Your attack rolls with Ranged weapons can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 17-20 on the d20.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain a special additional Bonus Action that you can take once on each of your turns. You can take this special Bonus Action only to use a maneuver.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Irresistible Offense](https://5e.tools/feats.html#boon%20of%20irresistible%20offense_xphb) is recommended.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: When you score a Critical Hit against a creature using a Ranged weapon, you can choose for it to be a Headshot. If the creature has less than 100 Hit Points, it dies. Otherwise, it takes an extra **10d10** damage of the weapon's type.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending three Risk (no action required).

description.name: Deadeye (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: *Shoot with Bullseye Precision*

A well-placed bullet is more powerful than a sword, arrow, or spell. Indeed, you believe that every violent conflict should sound like a single loud crack followed by a long silence. Such shots demand perfection, even at range, for when they are done right, they are as deadly for the target as they are stupendous for the audience.
__Eagle Eye [Maneuver] (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: Once per turn when you miss with a ranged attack roll, you can expend one Risk and add it to the attack roll, potentially causing the attack to hit.
__Sharpshooter's Stance (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: You have trained to fire from a stable Prone position, granting the following conditions.

description.name: Fire While Prone
description.value: You don't have Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls as a result of the Prone condition.

description.name: Quick Stand
description.value: When you have the Prone condition, you can right yourself and thereby end the condition with only 5 feet of movement.
Once per turn when you miss with a ranged attack roll, you can expend one Risk and add it to the attack roll, potentially causing the attack to hit.
You have trained to fire from a stable Prone position, granting the following conditions.

description.name: Fire While Prone
description.value: You don't have Disadvantage on ranged attack rolls as a result of the Prone condition.

description.name: Quick Stand
description.value: When you have the Prone condition, you can right yourself and thereby end the condition with only 5 feet of movement.

description.name: Deadeye (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: You excel at firing from concealment, granting you the following benefits.

description.name: Camouflage
description.value: You can take the Hide action even if you aren't Heavily Obscured or behind Three-Quarters Cover or Total Cover, as long as you have the Prone condition. The Invisible condition of this Hide action ends if you don't have the Prone condition.

description.name: Sniper's Nest
description.value: If you make an attack roll while hidden and the roll misses, making the attack roll doesn't reveal your location.

description.name: Deadeye (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Whenever a creature misses you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to end the Prone condition on yourself and move up to half your Speed.

description.name: Deadeye (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: When you take the Attack action, you can choose to make only one ranged attack roll using a weapon to make a Focused Shot. You have Advantage on this attack roll and, on a hit, score a Critical Hit.

description.name: High Roller (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: *Gamble with Life and Death*

Fortune is a fickle thing—unless you're a High Roller. These Gunslingers are master card sharps and dice throwers that mix their love of risk with their talent for gunplay. High Rollers push their luck until it runs out, then push harder. Why settle for a win when you could bet it all and win big?
__Poker Face (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: You gain proficiency with all Gaming Sets and in one of the following skills of your choice: *Deception*, *Insight*, or *Perception*.

__Liar's Dice [Maneuver] (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: When you make a damage roll with a Ranged weapon, you can expend one Risk as a Bonus Action and declare it to be a hidden roll. Roll the damage in secret and declare any total you wish. The GM has the option to call your bluff, in which case you reveal the damage dice you rolled. This has different consequences based on whether or not you lied.

description.name: The GM Calls Your Bluff; You Lied
description.value: The damage you deal is halved.

description.name: The GM Calls Your Bluff; You Told the Truth
description.value: The damage you deal is doubled.

description.name: The GM Doesn't Call Your Bluff
description.value: Use the total damage you declared, even if you rolled a different total.

When you make a damage roll with a Ranged weapon, you can expend one Risk as a Bonus Action and declare it to be a hidden roll. Roll the damage in secret and declare any total you wish. The GM has the option to call your bluff, in which case you reveal the damage dice you rolled. This has different consequences based on whether or not you lied.

description.name: The GM Calls Your Bluff; You Lied
description.value: The damage you deal is halved.

description.name: The GM Calls Your Bluff; You Told the Truth
description.value: The damage you deal is doubled.

description.name: The GM Doesn't Call Your Bluff
description.value: Use the total damage you declared, even if you rolled a different total.
You gain proficiency with all Gaming Sets and in one of the following skills of your choice: *Deception*, *Insight*, or *Perception*.

description.name: High Roller (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Once per turn when you make an attack roll against an enemy and the roll doesn't have Disadvantage, you can choose to make the roll with Disadvantage. When you do, you regain one expended Risk.

description.name: High Roller (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: You can use your Maverick Spirit and Skin of Your Teeth maneuvers without expending a Risk. When you do so, roll a d6 instead of a Risk.

description.name: High Roller (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: When you score a Critical Hit using a Ranged weapon, you can gamble for a higher result. Roll a d20. If the roll is a 10 or higher, roll all of the attack's damage dice four times and add them together, instead of only two times as normal for a Critical Hit. If you roll a 9 or lower on the d20, the Critical Hit becomes a normal hit.

description.name: Secret Agent (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: *Engage in Espionage and Assassination*

Knowledge is power. The best way to defeat your enemies is by stealing what they know and replacing it with misinformation. To that end, you have been trained in the ways of covert warfare, giving you a broad range of abilities to complement your fearsome gunnery skills.
__Operative Training (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: Your covert training grants you the following benefits:

description.name: Concealed Shot
description.value: You learn the __Concealed Shot__ cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip (choose when you select this subclass).

description.name: Operative Tools
description.value: You gain a Disguise Kit and Thieves' Tools, and you have proficiency with them.

description.name: Skill Proficiencies
description.value: You gain proficiency in two of these skills of your choice: *Deception*, *Investigation*, *Persuasion*, *Sleight of Hand*, or *Stealth*.

__Parting Shot [Maneuver] (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: When you take the Dash, Disengage, or Dodge action on your turn, you can expend one Risk to make a ranged attack using a weapon as a Bonus Action. Add the Risk to the damage roll on a hit.
Your covert training grants you the following benefits:

description.name: Concealed Shot
description.value: You learn the __Concealed Shot__ cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip (choose when you select this subclass).

description.name: Operative Tools

description.name: Skill Proficiencies

When you take the Dash, Disengage, or Dodge action on your turn, you can expend one Risk to make a ranged attack using a weapon as a Bonus Action. Add the Risk to the damage roll on a hit.

description.name: Secret Agent (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Your experience in the field grants you the following benefits.

description.name: Quick Change
description.value: Using a Disguise Kit, you can create a Costume and don it as a Bonus Action.

description.name: Slick Talker
description.value: Whenever you make a Charisma (*Deception*) or Charisma (*Persuasion*) check, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

description.name: Secret Agent (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to evade further harm. You have the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn, and you can immediately move up to 10 feet.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending one Risk (no action required).

description.name: Secret Agent (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Whenever you deal damage with a Ranged weapon, you can expend either one or two Risk and add them to the damage roll. If you roll the highest number on a Risk, you can roll the die again and add it to the damage without expending it, rolling again if it is the highest number again, and so on. The maximum number of Risk you can add to the damage equals your Proficiency Bonus.

description.name: Spellslinger (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: *Complement Your Gunslinging with Arcana*

Magic and guns aren't so different—arcane power is like gunpowder, a spell is like a bullet, and you are like a gun, directing your spells with precision at unfortunate targets. Spellslingers mix the disciplines of gunplay and spellcasting, sometimes loading arcane charges with your shots and firing bullets enhanced with lighting, frost, or flame.
__Spellcasting (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: You complement your bullets with the ability to cast spells.

description.name: Cantrips
description.value: You know two cantrips of your choice from the Wizard spell list (see that class's section for its list). __Fire Bolt__ and __Message__ are recommended. Whenever you gain a Gunslinger level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Wizard spell list.
When you reach Gunslinger level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

description.name: Spell Slots
description.value: The Spellslinger Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

description.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
description.value: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the Wizard spell list. __Chromatic Orb__, __Jump__, and __Shield__ are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Gunslinger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Spellslinger Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Wizard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Gunslinger, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
Changing your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Gunslinger level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

description.name: Spellcasting Ability
description.value: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

description.name: Spellcasting Focus
description.value: You can use an Arcane Focus or a Ranged weapon as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.
__Bang, You're Dead! (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: You can use magic in place of guns.

description.name: Finger Guns
description.value: You learn the __Finger Guns__ cantrip.

description.name: Arcane Shot
description.value: When you hit a target with a __Finger Guns__ attack, you can expend one Risk as a Bonus Action and add it to the damage roll.
You can use magic in place of guns.

description.name: Finger Guns
description.value: You learn the __Finger Guns__ cantrip.

description.name: Arcane Shot
description.value: When you hit a target with a __Finger Guns__ attack, you can expend one Risk as a Bonus Action and add it to the damage roll.

description.value: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the Wizard spell list. __Chromatic Orb__, __Jump__, and __Shield__ are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Gunslinger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Spellslinger Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Wizard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Gunslinger, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
Changing your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Gunslinger level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

description.name: Spellcasting Ability
description.value: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

description.name: Spellcasting Focus
description.value: You can use an Arcane Focus or a Ranged weapon as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

description.name: Spellslinger (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Wizard cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

description.name: Spellslinger (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Your experience in combating spellcasters grants you the following benefits.

description.name: Abjuration-Breaker
description.value: Whenever you make a ranged attack roll, you temporarily disrupt protective magic affecting the target. For the duration of the attack, the effects of spells targeting the creature, such as __Mage Armor__, as well as the properties and powers of magic items worn or carried by the creature, are suppressed and don't function. The target of the attack can't take a Reaction to cast spells such as __Shield__ in response to the attack or damage.

description.name: Antimagic Shot
description.value: When you score a Critical Hit and the target is affected by your Gut Shot feature, it also impedes the target's ability to cast spells. While the projectile is lodged in the target, it can't cast spells or take the Magic action. Additionally, the target has Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws it makes to maintain *Concentration*.

description.name: Inured to Magic
description.value: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can take a Reaction to roll 1d6 and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.

description.name: Spellslinger (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: When you make a spell attack roll, you can expend one Risk as a Bonus Action to substitute the spell attack with a ranged attack using a weapon. Add the Risk to the attack roll. On a hit, the attack deals the weapon's normal damage, in addition to the effects of the spell attack roll.

description.name: Trick Shot (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: *Ricochet Bullets from Every Angle*

Accuracy means different things to different people. For you, true accuracy isn't necessarily in hitting a target on the first shot, but might include hitting the mark after the bullet bounces around a dozen times. Your attacks are just as dangerous if they miss, or even after hitting their mark, as others' are while they're still in the air.
__Creative Trajectory (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: You can make your projectiles travel in unexpected ways. Your ranged attacks with weapons ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover.

__Ricochet [Maneuver] (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: When you miss with a ranged attack using a weapon, you can take a Bonus Action and expend one Risk to reroll the attack and add the Risk to the roll. You must use the new roll.
You can make your projectiles travel in unexpected ways. Your ranged attacks with weapons ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover.
When you miss with a ranged attack using a weapon, you can take a Bonus Action and expend one Risk to reroll the attack and add the Risk to the roll. You must use the new roll.

description.name: Trick Shot (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Your flashy weapon tricks grant you the following benefits.

description.name: Gun Spinning
description.value: Once per turn when you make a Charisma (*Performance*) check or a Dexterity (*Sleight of Hand*) check using one of your Ranged weapons, you can roll a Risk and add it to the ability check without expending it.

description.name: Speed Loader
description.value: On your turn, you can reload a weapon with Reload without taking an action or Bonus Action.

description.name: Trick Shot (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: You can shoot projectiles out of the air. When an ally within 30 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction and expend one Risk to grant that ally the benefit of the Skin of Your Teeth maneuver against that attack. You must be holding a Ranged weapon to use this maneuver.

description.name: Trick Shot (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a ranged attack using a weapon, you can deflect the projectile at additional targets. Choose a different target within 30 feet of the first and make an attack roll against it. On a hit, you can repeat this attack against a new target within 30 feet until you miss or make a total of five attacks. You can't target the same creature with more than one attack each time you use this feature.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending two Risk (no action required).

description.name: White Hat (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: *Protect Your Allies and Uphold the Law*

Some Gunslingers live by a code and expect others to do the same. These Gunslingers, known as White Hats, sometimes serve as officers of the law but never hesitate to do what's right when the law says otherwise. Despite their affinity for deadly weapons, White Hats prefer to keep their friends safe and subdue their enemies nonviolently—a preference their enemies don't often oblige.

__Lay Down The Law [Maneuver] (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: You can take a Bonus Action and expend one Risk to keep an eye out for dangers that threaten your companions. Choose an ally that you can see within 60 feet of you. That ally gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the Risk. Until the start of your next turn, if the ally is hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction to make a ranged attack using a weapon against the attacker.

__Steely-Eyed Aura (VALDAGUNSLINGER)__: An aura of stoic confidence radiates from you in a 10-foot Emanation. You and allies within the Emanation have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Frightened condition. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition.

name: Lay Down the Law [Maneuver] (Lv. 3 White Hat)

description.value: You can take a Bonus Action and expend one Risk to keep an eye out for dangers that threaten your companions. Choose an ally that you can see within 60 feet of you. That ally gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the Risk. Until the start of your next turn, if the ally is hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction to make a ranged attack using a weapon against the attacker.

An aura of stoic confidence radiates from you in a 10-foot Emanation. You and allies within the Emanation have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Frightened condition. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition.

name: Reach for the Skies (Lv. 6 White Hat)

description.name: White Hat (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: When you score a Critical Hit against a creature, you call for the target to surrender instead of lodging a projectile in it. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Maneuver save DC or have the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions for 1 minute. These conditions end early if the creature takes any damage, if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die. The creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the conditions on itself on a success.

name: Long Arm of the Law (Lv. 10 White Hat)

description.name: White Hat (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a ranged attack using a weapon, you can hobble the target. The creature can't move on its next turn unless it first takes the Disengage action.

description.name: White Hat (VALDAGUNSLINGER) Features
description.value: Though gunslinging heroism, you gain the following benefits.

description.name: Improved Aura
description.value: The range of your __Steely-Eyed Aura__ feature increases to 30 feet.

description.name: Iron-Clad Law
description.value: When you use your __Lay Down the Law [Maneuver]__ maneuver, the ally has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Stunned Surrender
description.value: When a creature fails its saving throw against your __Reach for the Skies__ feature, it has the Stunned condition instead of the Incapacitated condition.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You create or inherit a repository of knowledge known as a Monster Grimoire. Each Monster Hunter carries a grimoire, a manual on dangerous creatures. A Monster Hunter's grimoire is an object entirely unique to each hunter. It may be a leather tome recovered from a dusty library with notes made in the margins, a set of blood-stained scrolls inherited from a previous hunter, or a precious stone with a communing spirit held within.

If a Monster Hunter ever loses a grimoire, the hunter has retained enough knowledge to not suffer immediate drawbacks. However, the hunter can't add to the grimoire until it is restored and therefore can't take another Monster Hunter level until a lost grimoire has been replaced. A grimoire can be recreated by spending 8 hours and 50 GP worth of materials such as books, scrolls, and ink.

Choose two types of creatures that you are specialized in hunting from the following list: Aberrations, Beasts, Celestials, Constructs, Dragons, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, Giants, Monstrosities, Oozes, Plants, or Undead.

You add your Proficiency Bonus to Intelligence and Wisdom checks you make that relate to the creature types in your grimoire. For example, if Undead are in your grimoire, you add your Proficiency Bonus to an Intelligence (*History*) check to recall lore about an Undead creature you're investigating or a Wisdom (*Medicine*) check to identify claw marks left on a corpse by an Undead creature. If you are already proficient in a skill when asked to make an Intelligence or Wisdom ability check relating to the monster types in your grimoire, you add double your Proficiency Bonus instead.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language based on the chart below. (You can add languages to this chart based on your own campaign world.)

Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longbows and Longswords. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.
When you reach certain Monster Hunter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Monster Hunter Features table.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice.

You have learned the most effective way to slay a monster is to strike its most vulnerable area at the right moment. Too early, and your attack glances away. Too late, and the monster may eviscerate you.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you targets you or another creature with a melee or ranged attack, you can take a Reaction before the attack roll to make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike against that creature.
If the attack misses, you regain the use of your Reaction.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain a Monster Hunter subclass of your choice. The Carver Guild, Devourer Guild, Occultist Guild, and Trapper Guild subclasses are detailed below. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monster Hunter levels. The guild you choose grants you features when you reach Monster Hunter levels 3, 7, 10, 15, and 18.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You learn the weaknesses of monsters so that you know exactly where to strike to inflict the most damage. You can add your Intelligence modifier to the attack and damage rolls of your weapons and Unarmed Strikes.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You have expanded your Monster Grimoire with your experience and knowledge.

You can select a third creature type to add to your Monster Grimoire from the following list: Aberrations, Beasts, Celestials, Constructs, Dragons, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, Giants, Monstrosities, Oozes, Plants, or Undead. You can't choose a creature type you have chosen before. All the benefits you gain from your Monster Grimoire now also apply to this new type.
Additionally, your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes against creature types in your Monster Grimoire can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You can rely on your knowledge to anticipate a monster's actions and summon your best defense.
Whenever a creature type in your Monster Grimoire forces you to make a saving throw, you can make an Intelligence saving throw in place of that saving throw instead.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: Your Monster Grimoire is further expanded by your encounters and studies.

You can select a fourth creature type to add to your Monster Grimoire from the following list: Aberrations, Beasts, Constructs, Celestials, Dragons, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, Giants, Monstrosities, Oozes, Plants, or Undead. You can't choose a monster type you have chosen before. All the benefits you gain from your Monster Grimoire now also apply to this new monster type.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You are experienced at navigating the threats that arise near a monster's lair. You have Advantage on saving throws and Resistance to the damage of lair actions and regional effects caused by creatures. In addition, you have Advantage on saving throws and Resistance to damage against the Legendary Actions of creature types in your Monster Grimoire.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You're able to coordinate with your allies to quickly slay dangerous monsters.

When you use Studied Response, choose a Friendly creature that can see or hear you. That creature can use its Reaction to make one attack with a weapon or Unarmed Strike against the creature that triggered your Studied Response. If the ally does not have their Reaction, they regain it but then must use it to make the attack. Your ally's attack occurs after yours but before the target creature rolls its own attack. This ability refreshes at the start of your turn.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

description.name: Class Features
description.value: You gain the ability to strike mortal blows against the creatures you have studied.

Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes against creature types in your Monster Grimoire can now score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18 through 20 on the d20. When you score a Critical Hit against a creature type in your Monster Grimoire, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. The DC equals the damage taken, up to a maximum DC of 30. On a failed save, the creature drops to 0 Hit Points. On a successful save, the creature takes the attack's normal damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

description.name: Carver (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: *Slay Monsters Fearlessly and Recklessly*

Since the beginning of time, the brave glared into danger's ferocious eyes and fought monsters. Those who survived were the ones smart enough to arm themselves properly and know precisely where to strike—or those who knew when to flee and return with a new plan.

Members of the Carver Guild are the Monster Hunters typically called upon when immediate danger threatens a settlement and there is no army or militia available. Carvers stride unflinchingly toward death, armed with years of training and the knowledge passed down from those before them.
__Equipped For Battle (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You gain training with Heavy armor.

__Close Quarters (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: Your skill in close combat enables you to inflict crushing blows while keeping your opponent off balance. When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon, you can take a Reaction to deal an extra **1d6** damage of the same type dealt by the weapon. That creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

Your skill in close combat enables you to inflict crushing blows while keeping your opponent off balance. When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon, you can take a Reaction to deal an extra **1d6** damage of the same type dealt by the weapon. That creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.
You gain training with Heavy armor.

description.name: Carver (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Frightened condition, and you are Immune to the Frightened condition caused by creature types in your Monster Grimoire.

Additionally, when you hit a creature with an attack as part of a Reaction, you can choose a Frightened creature within 60 feet that can see you (including yourself). The condition ends on that creature.

description.name: Carver (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: Your reputation has become such that monsters preying on the fearful have come to fear you. When you hit a creature with an attack as part of a Reaction, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. The DC for the saving throw equals 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and your Proficiency Bonus.

description.name: Carver (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: Your strikes have become even deadlier. The extra damage of your Close Quarters increases to 3d6. In addition, if you deal damage to a creature with Close Quarters, the target has Disadvantage on all attack rolls until the end of your next turn.

description.name: Carver (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You are such an effective combatant that you are always in control and never off balance. You can take a Reaction twice in a round instead of once.

description.name: Devourer (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: *Gain Power by Consuming Monster Flesh*

Folk in Etharis don't always speak highly of Monster Hunters, and many consider them to be just as depraved and inhuman as the evils they vanquish. Many of the appalling tales about Monster Hunters can be attributed, directly or indirectly, to the Devourer Guild, who are accused of being monstrous cannibals.

The truth is barely any better. Devourers have spent their days consuming the flesh and blood of the monsters they slay, and, over time, their metabolism has changed to tolerate this disgusting practice. Devourers adopt mutations shortly after consuming their prey.
__Alchemical Gastronomy (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies and Cook's Utensils.

__Transmuting Metabolism (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You gain the ability to consume monster remains, which causes your body to adopt powerful and frightening mutations. These appear in the "Mutations" section later in the subclass's description.
Mutations
The mutations are presented here in alphabetical order, with required creature types shown in brackets after the mutation's name.
Acid Blood (Aberration, Ooze, Plant) (GrimHollowPG24)
Acumen (Celestial, Fiend, Fey) (GrimHollowPG24)
Awareness (All) (GrimHollowPG24)
Flight (Celestial, Dragon, Elemental) (GrimHollowPG24)
Infused (Dragon, Elemental, Ooze) (GrimHollowPG24)
Invisibility (Fey, Fiend, Undead) (GrimHollowPG24)
Might (Beast, Construct, Giant) (GrimHollowPG24)
Natural Weapons (Beast, Dragon, Monstrosity) (GrimHollowPG24)
Regeneration (Beast, Giant, Monstrosity) (GrimHollowPG24)
Resistance (Construct, Elemental, Undead) (GrimHollowPG24)
Telepathy (Aberration, Fiend, Plant) (GrimHollowPG24)

description.name: Salvaging Portions
description.value: As a Utilize action, you can harvest a single portion from the physical remains of a creature. Only one portion can be harvested from each creature. Record the monster's creature type. A harvested portion lasts until you finish a Long Rest, at which point it loses its potency.

description.name: Consuming Portions
description.value: As a Bonus Action, you can consume a portion. After you consume the portion, you choose a mutation to gain, depending on the creature's type. You can gain the benefits of consumed portions a number of times up to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). When you finish a Long Rest, you regain the ability to safely consume portions.
You can benefit from multiple portions simultaneously, but you can't gain the same mutation more than once at the same time.
You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies and Cook's Utensils.

description.name: Devourer (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: Your ingestion of monsters heightens your understanding of them and their behaviour. You gain this additional effect when you consume a monster portion: For 1 minute, when you make an attack as part of a Reaction, you deal an extra **1d6** damage. This damage has the same type as the weapon or Unarmed Strike used for the attack.

description.name: Devourer (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: Your hunger for your enemy allows you to partake of its essence during battle. When you deal damage to a creature with a melee attack using a weapon or Unarmed Strike, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt. If the target is a creature type in your Monster Grimoire, you instead gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the damage dealt instead.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

description.name: Devourer (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You can spend 1 hour and 20 GP worth of alchemical ingredients (such as special herbs or monster salvage) to use your Alchemist's Supplies to convert a monster portion into a decoction. A decoction is a magic potion that grants the benefits of a consumed monster portion. You can have 4 unconsumed decoctions active. You can destroy a decoction as a Utilize action.

A creature other than you can consume 1 decoction without adverse effects. A creature gains 1 Exhaustion level for each decoction it consumes after the first. A creature must finish a Long Rest before it regains the ability to safely consume a decoction.

description.name: Devourer (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: Your hunger for monster portions has increased to the point of being insatiable. You can now consume 1 additional portion safely. Additionally, for 1 minute when you consume a portion, you have Advantage, on attack rolls made as part of a Reaction.

description.name: Occultist (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: *Hunt Mages and Magical Adversaries*

In Etharis, there are those who fear magic, and those who seek to understand it. Monster Hunters from the Occultist Guild know folk from both sides are equally dangerous. An Occultist investigates the arcane, the supernatural, and the uncanny, while avoiding the influence of superstition or ideology. Despite their reputation as mage hunters, Occultists don't burn their enemies at the stake—Occultists put them to the sword, as that's what swords are for. Knowledge and magic give Occultists an edge over their mystical adversaries. Their spells are used to detect and defend against dangerous arcana, and, above all, magic is used to destroy monsters that can't be harmed by steel.
__Acolyte Of The Occult (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You gain proficiency in the *Arcana* skill.
__Spellcasting (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: Your study of the occult gives you the ability to cast spells.

description.name: Cantrips
description.value: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Wizard spell list. Whenever you gain a Monster Hunter level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another of your choice from the Wizard spell list.
When you reach Monster Hunter level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

description.name: Spell Slots
description.value: The Occultist Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

description.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
description.value: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Wizard spells. __Burning Hands__, __Detect Magic__, and __Protection from Evil and Good__ are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Monster Hunter levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Occultist Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Wizard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Monster Hunter, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

description.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
description.value: Whenever you gain a Monster Hunter level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell.

description.name: Spellcasting Ability
description.value: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

description.name: Spellcasting Focus
description.value: You can use an Arcane Focus as Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

__Arcane Interference (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creature types in your Monster Grimoire. Additionally, when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell or makes a spell attack, you can use Studied Response against that creature before the spell is cast.
You gain proficiency in the *Arcana* skill.

description.name: Occultist (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You consider Humanoids that can cast spells as being a creature type in your Monster Grimoire.
Additionally, when you damage a creature type in your Monster Grimoire that is *Concentrating*, it has Disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain its *Concentration*.

description.name: Occultist (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: Your knowledge of magic has increased so that you learn to cast Rituals. You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and it's a spell you have prepared.

In addition, you learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof (see a class's section for its spell list). A spell you choose must have the Ritual tag.
When you reach Monster Hunter level 14, you can replace one of the spells you know from this feature with another spell of your choice from any spell list. The new spell must have the Ritual tag.

description.name: Occultist (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You gain the ability to extend a protective charm. You radiate an unseeable aura in a 20-foot Emanation that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition. You and allies in your aura have Advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creature types in your Monster Grimoire.

Additionally, you always have the __Counterspell__ spell prepared. You can cast __Counterspell__ once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a Long Rest.

description.name: Occultist (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You have learned to anticipate your enemies well enough to rapidly cast spells in response to their attacks. When you use Studied Response, you can cast a spell. The spell must have a casting time of an action and must target only that creature.

description.name: Trapper (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: *Dispatch Monsters with Cunning Traps*

Legends say that the founding members of the Trapper Guild were game hunters who had grown bored of stalking common elk and dreamed of taking down bigger game. Trappers take pride in their kills and the ingenuity exhibited when a trap works perfectly.

The legacy of the Trapper Guild is a consistent testament to the benefits of lying in wait. The element of surprise is paramount to the trapper, whose kit can flourish before the hunter and monster even meet. Preparation is key, and the resourceful trapper has devices to assist in bringing down even the strongest foes.
__Sneaky And Crafty (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You gain proficiency in the *Stealth* skill and with Tinker's Tools.
__Trapper Gadgets (GRIMHOLLOWPG24)__: You learn to create gadgets and mechanisms that help you during the hunt.

As part of a Long Rest, you can craft two Trapper Gadgets if you have materials and Tinker's Tools on hand. Also, with 1 hour of work with such a kit and expending 20 GP worth of materials (such as equipment or monster salvage), you can create one Trapper Gadget from the list below.
Some Trapper Gadgets allow your target to make an ability check or saving throw to resist the gadget's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
• *Trapper Gadgets Save DC*: Intelligence modifier + Proficiency Bonus

description.name: Trapper (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You have become a ferocious ambusher. When you roll Initiative, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the roll. Additionally, you can't be *surprised* by enemies that inlcude creature types in your Monster Grimoire.

description.name: Trapper (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You can leap aside to avoid enemies rushing toward you. When a creature makes a melee attack roll against you, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on that roll and use your Studied Response as part of the same Reaction. Whether the attack hits or misses, you can then move up to half your Speed. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

description.name: Trapper (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You have learned to craft a set of Light or Medium armor by using dragon scales, werewolf hide, troll leather, or a similar monster component. The armor takes on the appearance of your choice, reflecting the component it is made from.

The armor has the same properties as Light or Medium armor (your choice when the armor is crafted) and gains two modifications from the Armor Modifications list. Whenever you gain a Monster Hunter level, you can replace one of these modifications with another modification.
Modifications require the armor to be worn to function.

description.name: Trapper (GRIMHOLLOWPG24) Features
description.value: You have become capable of crafting trapper tools at a much faster rate. You can spend 1 minute to make a Trapper Gadget without spending GP or components.
You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
